chapter: Hutto 1978-79: NBC, radio and the N'goma drums
title: Howard Lanin, Don Voorhees and joining NBC
summary: Hutto lists his late-1920s recording and NBC work; Nat Shilkret is named as the director he worked for most, and he made many records with Victor Young.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well I guess we're about ready to jump to that period. After the Goldkette Band, you more or less went into - I guess you made a few records with Howard Lanin.
And the Hit of the Week, the paper record, the paid for records.
And at that time about the late twenties, you got with NBC.
Now who were the more or less useful directors there, Frank Black or Nat Schilkret or anybody like that?

Nat Schilkret was one of them. And although he didn't know jazz at all. He'd have to take our word for what's good jazz. So Nat Schilkret, I think was the - I worked for him more than anyone else. He liked me, on account of my easy going way, my pace. He liked my pace. So that was it.
Now did you make records with Victor Young and the Brunswick orchestra?
